transcription.tex: 11. Robin claims\[\sum_{r=1}^n\frac{2r+1}{r(r+1)}=1-\frac1{n+1}\]Explain the error in using the method of differences here.

\[\frac{2r+1}{r(r+1)}=\frac1r+\frac1{r+1}\]The partial fractions are added, not subtracted. Successive terms do not cancel.\par For example, when \(n=1\), the sum is \(3/2\), whereas the claimed expression is \(1/2\).

transcription.tex: \textbf{Higher derivatives}\par Differentiate repeatedly. The second derivative is the derivative of the first derivative.

\[f(x),\quad f^{\prime}(x),\quad f^{\prime\prime}(x),\quad f^{(n)}(x)\]\[\frac{dy}{dx},\quad\frac{d^2y}{dx^2},\quad\frac{d^ny}{dx^n}\]Newton notation \(\dot y,\ddot y\) is commonly used for derivatives with respect to time.

transcription.tex: \textbf{From derivatives to polynomials}\par Can a polynomial reproduce the value and derivatives of a function at a chosen point?
At \(x=0\), the coefficients of \(a+bx+cx^2+dx^3+\cdots\) determine its successive derivatives.\[f(0)=a,\quad f^{\prime}(0)=b\]\[f^{\prime\prime}(0)=2c,\quad f^{\prime\prime\prime}(0)=6d\]

slides.title: Why we might represent functions as power series

transcription.tex: \textbf{Why use power series?}\par Polynomials are easy to evaluate, differentiate and integrate.\par A series can approximate functions near a chosen point.
Applications include numerical integration, approximating constants and solving differential equations.\[\arctan x=x-\frac{x^3}{3}+\frac{x^5}{5}-\cdots\]At \(x=1\), this gives a series for \(\pi/4\).

transcription.tex: 10. Find the Maclaurin expansion of \(\tan x\), up to and including \(x^5\).

Use \(f^{\prime}=1+f^2\) and differentiate repeatedly. At zero:\[f=0,\ f^{\prime}=1,\ f^{\prime\prime}=0\]\[f^{\prime\prime\prime}=2,\ f^{(4)}=0,\ f^{(5)}=16\]\[\tan x=x+\frac{x^3}3+\frac{2x^5}{15}+\cdots\]
